title: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports
license: No licence stated; facts only (dates, names, the kind of work done). Every note is our own wording and every event links to the FFLA report it comes from. Positions are copied from the NHLR, FFLOS and FFLA records.

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for the Crossroads tower to the city of Hamburg; phase one covers replacing guy cables, repairing footings, and fixing wooden steps and landings.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A 60-foot steel stair tower with a dwelling and garage was built in Shawnee National Forest in 1934; only the footers remain.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The tower in Shawnee National Forest was closed in October 2020 while repairs were made to protective fencing atop it; work to continue into 2021.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: With federal stimulus (ARRA) money, the Ferdinand State Forest tower got new treated-wood steps and railing fencing in summer 2009.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The current Henryville tower was built in 1928; an older 25-foot hardwood lookout had stood on a nearby knoll.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Tower was repainted to cover graffiti, but vandals promptly tagged its sides again.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Tower at Morgan Monroe State Forest was taken down and restored with ARRA funds and Young Hoosier Conservation Corps labor, led by Jeremy Kolaks; completed in 2010.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The 86-foot steel tower with a 7x7-foot cab was built in 1935 by Civilian Conservation Corps Company 589.
The Friends of McCormick's Creek State Park raised over $100,000 to restore the 1935 tower and reopened it to the public with a ribbon cutting; the cab is open on guided days.
The new plaza at the tower's base was finished as the last piece of the restoration; the tower is fully reopened to climbers.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The 100-foot galvanized steel tower was built in 1939 by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
Restoration, begun in spring 2017 with funds raised by the park friends group, was completed and the tower reopened to the public in spring 2018.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded ($500) for repairing the fire-damaged Tater Knob tower cab; local groups also raised about $2,000 at a benefit concert.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Because a highway widening put it in the right-of-way, the Mosley Hill tower was dismantled on Feb 1, 2006 and moved in pieces to a site near its new location.
The Mosley Hill tower was re-erected on July 13, 2007 at its new location.
In May 2007 a Kisatchie National Forest Passport in Time project rebuilt the vandalism-burned cab floor, straightened window frames and repainted the cab.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for Mosley Hill tower: replacing cab glass, repairing metal window frames, and cleaning and waterproofing the cab.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state forest fire control maintenance crew replaced the stair platforms.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew inspected the tower to judge whether repairs would be needed in future.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew repaired minor vandalism damage.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew replaced the whole tower cab with a rebuilt one.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew installed a new antenna on the tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew installed new landing platforms.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew replaced the floor and a wall inside the cab.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The closed Waltham tower was sold by the state to a private buyer, with the chapter director's help, and moved to Tennessee.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state maintenance crew completed new electrical wiring to the cab and the tower lines.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Old watchman's camp (observer cabin) on the summit was removed in summer 2011; the tower itself was still standing and recommended for removal by the state.
The Mount Abraham tower was blown over in high winds and was left lying on the summit; it was the only tower loss in the year.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A volunteer team led by Roger Morneault spent November 9-11, 2007 replacing guy lines, hardware, anchors and the roof and removing old antennas on the cab.
Follow-up work on the Allagash Mountain tower in 2008 added new paint and two new footings after the late-2007 repairs, led by Roger Morneault.
Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands had a new cab airlifted onto the original steel in August 2020, one of three cabs replaced that week.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Maine Parks and Lands burned the 1905-site lookout on site on 15 April, citing liability, vandalism and sensitive alpine vegetation; the second and last 1905 site lost.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Clear Lake lookout in T10 R11 was removed.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Maine Public Lands Division renovated the watchman's camp so it can serve as a shelter and picnic area, with Maine Forest Service helicopter help.
The tower lost its cab in 2019, leaving bare steel; planning for repair or replacement began without a completion date.
A new cab was helicoptered onto Deboullie Mountain tower in August 2020 by Maine Parks and Lands after the cab was lost in 2019.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Grand Lake Stream Fire Tower, an enclosed wooden tower on Downeast Lakes Land Trust property, was built in 1934.
Structural architects and Maine Cabin Masters contractors assessed the Grand Lake Stream tower and found it non-salvageable and dangerous; removal was planned for late fall 2025 but had not occurred.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Harris Mountain lookout was removed in 2006; FFLA later helped document its history in a Dixmont centennial book.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The lookout cab was removed and a new observation deck was built in its place.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Steel-only tower was removed for the MSCommNet radio tower and judged not salvageable.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Minor winter damage to the Mount Agamenticus tower was repaired in 2007 with help from the York fire chief and his members.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for the Mount Agamenticus tower restoration (complete stair and landing replacement, cab and catwalk repairs, new windows); the report cites a $500 grant.
The tower stayed closed for the whole 2016 fire season because of its poor condition, pending restoration.
The engineering study of the tower was completed, with recommended adjustments; radio equipment had to be moved before repairs could start.
The tower is closed because of the cab replacement effort and will not open in 2020.
The rotted cab was taken off the 1940s steel tower, which still stands without a cab.
The remaining steel was taken down in December 2025 because deteriorated footings and steel made it unsafe; a steering committee is weighing what comes next.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Old steel remains of the tower were removed in early September for the radio project; no one wanted the two bare steel sections, so they were scrapped.
New fire-tower look-alike, with a dummy cab hiding radio antennas and a public observation platform, was finished on the summit in July, replacing the scrapped steel tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A private buyer had Haskell Hill tower in Jefferson dismantled by Rockport Steel and barged to Lasell Island, where he is re-erecting it.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

records.name: Norway Bluff Lookout (now at the Ashland Logging Museum)

events.note: Tower was taken off its mountain on 7 May and moved to the Ashland Logging Museum on 13 June as a static display, with help from museum and Maine Forestry staff.
At the museum site a volunteer carpenter was repairing the display: concrete pad in place, steel frame newly painted, reconditioned wood cab ready to be set on top.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The stairs of the Ossipee Hill tower were repainted in 2008.
After a summer break-in at the tower was found by an FFLA member, the local fire department made repairs.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for materials to replace cracked and rotted braces, cross members and hardware on the tower's wooden superstructure.
FFLA members, helped by an FFLA grant, replaced the worst rotted and cracked braces in the tower's wooden superstructure.
Volunteers replaced some lower leg ties in October using lumber donated by Moulton Lumber; John Moulton and steward Ken Kennedy did the work.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Aroostook Riders ATV Club, now the tower's stewards, replaced all stairs and landings in summer 2008, with railing and paint still to come.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The cabless Priestly Mountain tower, which held state radio gear, was removed in July 2009 after Homeland Security built a new radio complex and steel tower at the site.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The lookout cab was blown off the tower in a wind storm, leaving the tower without a cab.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Maine Public Lands carried out footing and guy line work; the state also built a new cab in its Ashland shop, to be installed in 2019.
A new cab was airlifted onto Round Pond Mountain tower in August 2020 in the same week-long Maine Parks and Lands project.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

records.name: Squaw Mountain Lookout (now at the Greenville Visitor Center)

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for Squaw Mountain tower: seed money to buy materials and hardware to rebuild the tower cab in Big Moose Township.
Tower (also called Squaw Mountain) was flown off the summit on 12 Oct by Maine Forest Service crews to the Natural Resource Education Center site on Route 15 in Greenville for rebuilding.
In fall 2011 the Maine Forest Service took the tower apart and flew it off the mountain, for restoration of the 1919 steel and a replica cab at the Department of Corrections.
Tower lying at the Natural Resource Education Center in Greenville was picked up in fall 2014 and delivered to the Charleston Correctional Facility shop for restoration with inmate labor.
The tower, with restored 1919 steel and a rebuilt cab, was re-erected at the Greenville visitor center after MaineDOT trucked it back.
A photo caption shows the 1919 tower after restoration in January 2015; plan is to rebuild the cab to the 1958 plans and re-erect it at the Greenville visitor center.
Restoration at the Greenville Visitors Center was finished and the tower was dedicated on August 13, 2016 and opened to the public.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for building a watchman's camp replica beside the relocated tower at the Greenville Visitors Center ($500 to the Natural Resource Education Center).
A volunteer team built the watchman's camp replica next to the tower at the Greenville Visitor Center; it was ready for the winter and awaited painting and interior work.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Two fall maintenance trips stabilized the tower and left it weather tight for the winter of 2013/2014.
The Wadleigh Mountain lookout in T1 R12 was removed; a 12-foot ladder section was later salvaged for the Squaw Mountain tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: New landowners (Sustainable Forest Technologies) cut down and dropped the Washington Bald tower in T42 MD in summer 2007 rather than keep it.
The watchman cabin at the former Washington Bald lookout was removed by the new landowners in early 2008.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Cab was removed from the tower, counted in the state survey as a cab removal rather than a full tower loss.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Planned helicopter lift on 19 May failed because the steel was too heavy and the cab too rotted, so the tower was cut down in pieces and scrapped for the MSCommNet radio tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The University of Minnesota hired an engineering firm to assess the safety of the tower's stairs and railings; the report was still pending.
In September a new 6-foot chain-link fence with a 4-foot door was installed at the base, replacing the damaged old fence.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for full rehabilitation: rust-proof paint, new wood stairs and bolts, missing windows, trap door repair, roof rehab and interpretive signs, led by Peter Barr.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The North Carolina Forest Service replaced the Duckett Top tower roof (the 2008 date comes from the grants report).
FFLA restoration grant awarded for repainting and upkeep of Duckett Top tower: the first emergency stabilization grant ($150), to new lookout steward Wes Greene.
Chapter member Wes Greene repainted the entire Duckett Top tower over several weekends in 2009, partly paid by an emergency stabilization grant.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for water-damage repairs (plywood over missing windows, new siding, flashing) to the Duckett Top tower; the grant was later returned in 2025 as the work was postponed.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for paint (a $150 emergency stabilization grant) to cover heavy graffiti on the tower on the Appalachian Trail.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for the Rich Mountain tower restoration project ($500 from the national FFLA program, supporting the project near Hot Springs, NC).
Restoration of the tower was completed with the Forest Service, Appalachian Trail Conservancy and Carolina Mountain Club; a ribbon cutting followed and the project drew over $100,000.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The NC chapter organized a 2009 group hike with Park Service staff to Shuckstack tower to examine its condition and discuss rehabilitation.
The chapter lists the rehabilitation of the Shuckstack lookout tower as a 2015 accomplishment; an announcement and media plan for the restoration was set for 2016.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Chapter member Charles Nuckolls of the Nantahala Hiking Club repaired the Wesser Bald tower in summer 2008, replacing many wooden stairs, railings and deck flooring.

events.note: Valley Crane Company erected a refurbished Aermotor tower behind a Bass Pro Shop in Hooksett early in 2022; it is fenced, closed to the public and lacks its first stair flight.

events.note: Rehabilitation, painting and new cab at the state tower, costing $712,000; cab walls and roof were airlifted into place, delayed by wet weather; operation expected 2024.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A new tower cab was installed on the Blue Job tower in 2008.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Rehabilitation, painting and new cab at the state tower, costing $436,000; cab walls and roof were airlifted into place, delayed by wet weather; operation expected 2024.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: New Hampshire's Forests and Lands replaced the tower cab on Croydon Peak in 2009 despite budget cuts.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: State-hired contractors did extensive rehabilitation, including installing a new cab on the tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A state contractor took down the Hyland Hill tower in early June 2020; it had been unused since 2005 and was decaying and vandalized, leaving one footing.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The cab on the Mount Magalloway tower was replaced in 2006.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state replaced the tower cab and did other work on the Mt. Kearsarge tower in 2019.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The state replaced the tower cab and did other work on the Oak Hill tower in 2019.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A new cab was installed and the tower was painted.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: White Mountain National Forest's Saco Ranger District made extensive repairs to the tower in late August and early September.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for scraping and painting the tower and cab plus other maintenance; grantee was the Moultonborough Fire Department; the Lakes Region Conservation Trust owns the land.
Watchman Ed Maheux and an assistant replaced the shingles on the roof of the tower cab.
Inspections in June and November found no work done and no attempt to paint the cab or steelwork, despite the earlier FFLA restoration grant.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: On 30 August the chapter director visited the tower and found only the long-standing problem of three of four non-functional guy cables; an engineer was to assess it in 2015.
White Mountain National Forest announced in August that the tower was closed to the public until critical repairs could be made for safe access.
Historicorps workers replaced the tower roof and installed a lightning protection system, and the Forest Service reopened the tower to the public.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Milton tower, out of service since Sandy cut its power and phone in 2012, was returned to service and staffed again in 2020.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Azure Mountain tower restoration was finished in summer 2003 and opened with a grand opening in August; Friends of Azure Mountain volunteers act as weekend guides.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The long-awaited engineering assessment of the closed observer's cabin museum was finished in 2025; repairs noted in a 2019 inspection still have no decision on how to proceed.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for completing restoration of the Beebe Hill tower and observer cabin (cabin interior to become a museum; bolts, railings, painting).
Wire safety meshing was installed around each landing platform of the Beebe Hill tower, in addition to the raised handrails.
Work began April 5, 2008 with Ironworkers Local 10: new bolts and nuts on the X-braces and handrails raised to 42 inches with mid-rails on all landings and stairways.
Tower closed pending repairs to its roof; by 2023 the report says it still awaited an engineering inspection.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for starting restoration of the Berry Hill observer cabin: new porch floor and railing, roof repairs, interior cleanup and varnish, vintage photos.
The restored Berry Hill tower reopened with a ribbon cutting on 13 September 2021, after NYSDEC secured funding for the work.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The tower was restored to near its historical appearance under a Wild Forest amendment; communications gear and a building under the tower were removed in the fall.
Major restoration work was done on Blue Mountain tower in 2019, with Team Rubicon volunteers partnering with the NY Chapter.
FFLA volunteers and the NYSDEC liaison restored the observer's cabin: new siding and windows, porch screening, sanded and stained interior, rodent-proofing.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The tower was re-erected on its original site, raising the chapter's count of standing New York towers to about 79.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Chapter volunteers spent a day on site painting this formerly private tower, which was being readied for public opening in 2023.
After the multi-year project to prepare it, the tower reopened to the public in September 2023.

records.name: Cornell Hill Lookout (now at Wilton/Camp Saratoga)

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for furnishing the cab of the relocated former Cornell Hill tower at Camp Saratoga with a map table, circular fire finder map and alidade.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded toward restoring the 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower, with new steps, landings, cab floor and safety screening, by Friends of Grafton Lakes State Park and FFLA-NY.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Tower (its cab) closed pending roof repairs; the 2023 report says the cab was still closed awaiting engineering inspection results.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A new roof and fresh paint, funded by a $48,000 Adventure NY grant, were completed in time for the centennial celebration.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The restoration project was completed and the tower reopened to the public.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The 80-foot tower was taken down in October 2016, the chapter's one loss of the year.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Major restoration work was carried out by FFLA and Team Rubicon.
Tower closed to the public pending an engineering inspection whose completion date was unknown; still closed in the 2023 report.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for repairs to the Kane Mountain observer's cabin, paid to the NY Chapter (the report mislabels the state as California).
Observer's cabin got a new roof and porch from NYSDEC staff, and FFLA volunteers stained the siding using grant-funded supplies.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Tower closed to the public pending an engineering inspection whose completion date was unknown; still closed in the 2023 report.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The 1916 Aermotor LL25 Makomis tower was unearthed and returned to fine condition; it awaits a new home, hoped to be in New York.
Historic Makomis tower was re-erected at a new Adirondack site in Speculator, planned with the village and FFLA volunteers; grand opening held September 1, 2022.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

records.name: Moosehead Mountain Lookout (now at Industry City)

events.note: The former Moosehead Mountain tower was re-erected in Brooklyn in October 2016 by Dave Vana of Davana LLC.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The former observer's cabin was moved by landowner D. Randall to his property, where it is to become a NYS Fire Tower Museum staffed by FFLA members; the museum project continues in 2026.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded to Friends of Mount Adams for tower paint, roof panels, windows, a firefinder map reproduction, and repairs to the 1922-type observer cabin.
The Friends of Mount Adams began restoring the observer cabin (the only surviving 1922 standard-design cabin) in summer 2007.
By 2008 the Mount Adams tower had been painted and given new wooden steps by DEC, while the 1922-type observer cabin got new footings and drainage in an ongoing restoration.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for Mount Beacon tower restoration (hardware, paint and materials; committee chaired by David Rocco); total cost over $10,000 over 2-3 years.
Restoration work began in October 2008 with installation of new stair treads and landing platforms.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

records.name: New Boston Lookout (now at the Thompson Park Zoo)

events.note: The tower, formerly the New Boston fire tower, was moved into Thompson Park Zoo in Watertown as a community education exhibit.
Thompson Park Zoo in Watertown restored the New Boston tower on its grounds; it stayed closed to the public until liability insurance could be secured.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for renovation of the Thompson Park Zoo tower in Watertown ($500 FFLA grant).
Renovation of the tower at Thompson Park Zoo was finished in spring 2016 despite weather difficulties.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Restoration of the Owl's Head tower near Long Lake was about half finished, with most work done by local forest ranger Jim Waters.
Owl's Head tower restoration was completed and the tower opened to the public, with most of the work done by the local ranger.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for Page Pond Hill tower and observer cabin (cab repainting, new floor, stair treads, landings, safety fencing; cabin roof and finish).
Cabin work began in fall 2007 (tree trimming, moss treatment, roof repair, staining and varnishing); FFLA members held a work party Oct 13-14 at the site.
Work days in 2008 continued restoration of the Page Pond Hill cabin and tower, including staining the cabin exterior and repairing a cabin window.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for Pillsbury Mountain tower facility, first to replace the failing observer cabin roof with NYS DEC staff.
Major restoration work took place on Pillsbury tower in 2019, with the remaining work to be finished in 2020.
FFLA volunteers finished replacing the tower's landing and step boards in 2021, with NYSDEC flying materials in by helicopter.
NYSDEC declared the observer's cabin surplus and burned it down in March 2025.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The Friends replaced the stolen brass alidade with a replica, in place for most of the hiking season, and upgraded security for the tower cab.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for replacing the tower's stolen brass alidade; the $200 Matt Walter Fund grant went to the Friends of Poke-O-Moonshine.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Newly formed Friends of Bald (Rondaxe) Mountain began restoring the tower by painting it in summer 2003, helped by FFLA member Ann Spaziano.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Restoration was completed and the tower reopened, with a new trail to the summit that is closed during hunting season under a conservation easement.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Restoration work was done in 2015; the project awaited delivery of some new steel pieces, with reopening expected in 2016.
The restored tower held a soft opening on September 1, 2016.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for work on the Sterling Forest tower: new steps and landings, cab window reglazing, railings and fencing, cab repainting and ground cabin repairs ($500).
All steps and landings were replaced, the cab was secured for winter, and the ground cabin was stained and cleaned; major work days were in July and November.
Tower closed to the public pending an engineering inspection whose completion date was unknown; still closed in the 2023 report.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded to the Friends of Stillwater Fire Tower toward total restoration of the 47-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower, in partnership with NYS DEC.
Restoration work was nearly finished in 2015; the friends group expected a grand reopening in spring 2016.
The restored tower officially reopened to the public on July 2, 2016.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for reconditioning rusted areas and structural joints of the 67-foot 1937 International Derrick tower, led by Bill Starr with NYSDEC Region 8; work set for September.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Warren County restored the tower and built a new trail; it reopened on 13 August 2021 with a grand opening.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for roof repairs on the 47-foot Aermotor tower; $500 to Warren County Parks, Recreation & Railroad toward roof materials and paint.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for restoration of the Mount Utsayantha tower (a $200 grant), the only NY tower to apply and receive one that year.
AmeriCorps workers from Delhi and FFLA members painted the Utsayantha tower in October 2004, while deputies worked on the cab.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A local group working with the state painted the Vanderwacker Mountain tower in summer 2003, with AmeriCorps students doing much of the work.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The tower was closed in December 2016 and later found to need emergency stabilization.
Emergency stabilization repairs were made in May 2017; further repairs could not be finished and were scheduled for spring 2018.
Major restoration work was carried out by NYSDEC and a private contractor.

records.name: Armintrout Fire Tower (now at the Ohio Exposition Center)

events.note: The former ODNR tower from Meigs County was moved to the Natural Resources Park at the Ohio State Fairgrounds in Columbus and shortened by 20 feet; the project cost $130,000.
The tower was fully disassembled, restored and rebuilt, and repainted in its original silver and orange.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

records.name: Snake Ridge Lookout Tower (now at the Wayne NF Headquarters)

events.note: Federally owned tower was moved and opened next to the Wayne National Forest headquarters after a few years of work, and was certified by FFLA.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: A new group of ham radio operators and emergency personnel re-roofed the tower in Scituate during 2022.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for the Nooseneck tower (work not specified); it was presented to the West Greenwich fire department at the 2005 eastern conference.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The same volunteer restoration group reconnected electrical power to the tower in Exeter in 2022.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Teens set fireworks off at the abandoned 1968 tower in Richmond on July 6, gutting the cab; the state was weighing full removal and replacement with a communications tower.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for a comprehensive condition assessment of the tower, the first step toward restoration, matched with a South Carolina SHPO grant.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded to Friends of the Smokies to repair weather and vandal damage: new first-floor door and hardware, paint over graffiti and a rotten spruce roof beam.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: FFLA restoration grant awarded for phase two of Pinnacle Mountain tower restoration: stair rehabilitation and treads, handrails, and added steel supports.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The tower and summit cabin in Westmore were restored in 2002.
Ranger's cabin on Bald Mountain in Westmore was restored in a major Northeast Kingdom project.
The Westmore tower had an extensive renovation in which all of its wooden components were replaced with white oak.
Interior cab railings were installed on the Westmore fire tower.
The summit cabin at the Westmore tower received a new metal roof.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: Wooden steps and landings on the Bear Hill lookout in Allis State Park were replaced with metal grates.
Tower maintenance at Allis State Park was completed, covering lightning protection, paint, interior cab railings and wire mesh on stairs and landings.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association chapter reports

events.note: The concrete steps at the Burke Mountain tower were repaired in 2007, but no work was done on the cab or tower itself.
Vermont state staff finished extensive renovation of the Burke Mountain tower, replacing all steps, landings and the cab floor with white oak on galvanized hardware.
A safety railing was added to the cab floor and metal fencing was installed along the sides, stairs and landings.
Tower maintenance was completed, covering lightning protection, paint, interior cab railings and wire mesh on stairs and landings (work listed jointly with Okemo and Bear Hill).

events.note: State Department of Forests and Parks repaired the loose step footings at the base of the tower, a repair needed for many years.
FFLA restoration grant awarded for restoring the Mt. Olga fire tower in southern Vermont ($500), with completion hoped for the following year.
All the glass windows in the cab were removed to prevent further vandal damage.
The tower now has a new steel grated stairway, making it more stable and less prone to ice buildup.
Interior cab railings were installed.
